newsitem.title: CHINA: Poll - China RPI, CPI seen rising in July.
newsitem.headline: Poll - China RPI, CPI seen rising in July.

text.p: China's retail and consumer inflation were expected to show a rise for July after prices bottomed out and bad weather boosted food prices, analysts polled by Reuters said.
Benchmark retail price inflation in July was expected to rise 1.07 percent year-on-year, compared with 0.8 percent in June, the analysts said.
Consumer price inflation was forecast at 3.17 percent year-on-year for July, compared with 2.8 percent in June, they said.
The State Statistical Bureau was expected to release the figures for July in the next few days.

An economist with DBS Securities said inflation had bottomed out and would start to show a slow rise although stable food prices due to the bumper summer grain crop would have a major stabilising effect on overall price levels.
However, an economist with Nikko Securities said disastrous weather conditions such as severe flooding in southern China would cause food prices to rise, pushing up price levels across the country.

Economists from Nomura Securities and DBS Securities said a rise in the cost of rent and electricity as well as other public services would be the main factor behind an increase in consumer price inflation.

In the first half of this year, large- and medium-sized Chinese cities adjusted rent and utility prices, raising rents by an average of 18.8 percent, water charges by 17.6 percent and electricity charges by 16.1 percent, figures from the China Price Information Centre showed.

However, analysts from Dresdner Kleinwort Benson Securities and Yamaichi Securities said they expected prices to continue to fall because growth in incomes was seen declining as state enterprises laid off more workers.
Average per capita urban income in the first half rose by a real 2.2 percent year-on-year, down 2.0 percentage points compared with the same period last year, State Statistical Bureau figures showed.
In the first half of this year, retail price inflation rose 1.8 percent year-on-year and consumer price inflation was 4.1 percent year-on-year.
